title: Finite-width plate with a central circular hole in tension (plane stress, quarter model)
description:
Long flat steel bar (strip) with a central circular through-hole, pulled along its length, plane stress. By double symmetry only the quarter x >= 0, y >= 0 is modelled (STEP: planar face in the xy-plane); the hole centre is at the origin.
Geometry: full bar width W = 0.2 m (y from -W/2 to W/2), hole diameter d = 0.1 m (d/W = 0.5), full length 0.8 m (x from -0.4 to 0.4 m). Quarter model: rectangle [0, 0.4] x [0, 0.1] m minus the quarter disk of radius 0.05 m. Edges: y = 0 (from (0.05, 0) to (0.4, 0)), x = 0.4 (loaded end), y = 0.1 (free side), x = 0 (from (0, 0.05) to (0, 0.1)), and the quarter-circle hole edge.
Material: linear elastic, E = 2e+11 Pa, nu = 0.3, thickness 0.002 m.
Loads: uniform tensile traction sigma0 = 1e+08 Pa (100 MPa) along +x on the end x = 0.4 m (gross-section stress). The side y = W/2 and the hole are free.
Supports: symmetry on x = 0 (u_x = 0) and on y = 0 (u_y = 0).
Report (SI units):
  s_peak   sigma_xx at the edge of the hole on the transverse axis, (0, 0.05) [Pa]
  vm_max   maximum von Mises stress [Pa]
